items.stem: Define the term 'marketing plan'.
items.answer: A detailed document setting out the marketing objectives, the strategies and marketing mix to achieve them, the budget, the timescale and how results will be measured.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, a detailed document setting out the marketing objectives, the strategies and marketing mix to achieve them, the budget, the timescale and how results will be measured. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why marketing objectives must be consistent with corporate objectives.
items.answer: Marketing objectives are a means of achieving corporate goals; if they conflict (e.g. a cheap volume strategy when the corporate goal is premium positioning) resources are wasted and the strategy fails.
items.markingKey: 1 mark link/hierarchy of objectives; 1 mark consequence of conflict. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of setting the marketing budget as a percentage of sales.
items.answer: Advantage: simple and affordable because it is linked to revenue. Disadvantage: spending falls when sales fall, just when more promotion may be needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each with explanation. [2]

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain how a detailed marketing plan could help IslaConnect launch AI chatbot services.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: a marketing plan sets objectives, strategy, budget and timescales; coordinates the marketing mix for the target segment; allocates the budget to the most effective activities; allows results to be measured against targets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a marketing plan sets objectives, strategy, budget and timescales. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for IslaConnect, e.g. coordinates the marketing mix for the target segment; allocates the budget to the most effective activities; allows results to be measured against targets. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Explain the factors Maple Learning should consider when setting its marketing budget.
items.answer: Points to develop for Maple Learning: marketing budget allocates spending to marketing; marketing objectives and the tasks needed; competitors' spending; available finance and expected return.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: marketing budget allocates spending to marketing. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Maple Learning, e.g. marketing objectives and the tasks needed; competitors' spending; available finance and expected return. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Accra, Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd (private limited company) buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. The business has around 450 employees. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Evaluate the most appropriate method for Gold Coast Cocoa to set its marketing budget.
items.answer: For: objective-and-task links spending to goals; percentage of sales is simple and affordable; competitor parity avoids losing share. Against: objective-and-task can be expensive; percentage of sales is pro-cyclical; competitor parity ignores own objectives. Judgement: the decision for Gold Coast Cocoa depends mainly on its marketing objectives, and also on its financial position.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Gold Coast Cocoa: confectionery, about 450 employees, private limited company in Ghana; world cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. objective-and-task links spending to goals; percentage of sales is simple and affordable; competitor parity avoids losing share; arguments against, e.g. objective-and-task can be expensive; percentage of sales is pro-cyclical; competitor parity ignores own objectives. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its marketing objectives; its financial position; the intensity of competition. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which is the best example of a SMART marketing objective?
options: Increase market share in Chile from 8% to 11% within 18 months
Become the best brand in the world
items.answer: Increase market share in Chile from 8% to 11% within 18 months
items.markingKey: Increase market share in Chile from 8% to 11% within 18 months. SMART objectives are specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound.

items.stem: A business with sales revenue of $8,000,000 sets its marketing budget at 6% of sales. What is the budget?

Kiwi Trails Ltd expects sales revenue of $8,000,000 next year and sets its marketing budget at 8% of forecast sales, split 35% digital advertising, 35% sales promotion, 20% trade shows, 10% public relations. Calculate the total budget and the amount for digital advertising.

IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Using the case and your own knowledge, discuss whether a marketing plan is essential for the success of IslaConnect.
items.answer: For: coordination and focus; measurable objectives and budget control; supports investment decisions. Against: markets change faster than plans; plans are only as good as their research; flexibility and creativity matter. Judgement: the decision for IslaConnect depends mainly on the speed of change in its market, and also on its size and resources.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. coordination and focus; measurable objectives and budget control; supports investment decisions; arguments against, e.g. markets change faster than plans; plans are only as good as their research; flexibility and creativity matter. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the speed of change in its market; its size and resources; how the plan is reviewed. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to IslaConnect, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Define the term 'research and development (R&D)'.
items.answer: The scientific and technical work carried out to create new products and processes or improve existing ones.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the scientific and technical work carried out to create new products and processes or improve existing ones. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why spending on R&D does not guarantee business success.
items.answer: Most projects fail to produce a viable product; R&D is costly and slow, and competitors may launch first or customers may not want the result.
items.markingKey: 1 mark uncertainty/failure rate; 1 mark cost/time or market risk. [2]

items.stem: Explain how new product development links to the product life cycle.
items.answer: New products replace those in decline and extend the portfolio, so the business always has products in growth to generate future cash flow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark replacing declining products; 1 mark balanced portfolio/cash flow. [2]

items.stem: A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Nusantara Apparel Tbk, a public limited company in Indonesia with about 4,000 employees, makes sportswear under contract for global brands. Explain how investing in research and development could improve the competitiveness of Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: R&D creates new products and processes; differentiation of sportswear allows premium pricing; process innovation lowers unit costs; patents give temporary protection from rivals.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: R&D creates new products and processes. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nusantara Apparel, e.g. differentiation of sportswear allows premium pricing; process innovation lowers unit costs; patents give temporary protection from rivals. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

Explain how investing in research and development could improve the competitiveness of IslaConnect.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: R&D creates new products and processes; differentiation of call-centre and back-office services allows premium pricing; process innovation lowers unit costs; patents give temporary protection from rivals.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: R&D creates new products and processes. items.stem: Lumen Robotics plc is a public limited company based in Singapore. It designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines and employs about 2,400 people. Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Discuss whether Lumen Robotics should launch robots for hospital logistics after a test market or launch it nationally at once.
items.answer: For: test market reduces risk; feedback improves the product; lower initial cost. Against: delay gives competitors time to copy; test area may not be representative; national launch gains first-mover advantage. Judgement: the decision for Lumen Robotics depends mainly on the strength of competition, and also on the cost of failure.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. test market reduces risk; feedback improves the product; lower initial cost; arguments against, e.g. delay gives competitors time to copy; test area may not be representative; national launch gains first-mover advantage. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the strength of competition; the cost of failure; how unique the product is. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Lumen Robotics, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Desert Bloom Hotels plc, a public limited company in the United Arab Emirates with about 3,100 employees, operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels. Explain one advantage to Desert Bloom of increasing its R&D spending to develop serviced apartments for long-stay guests.
items.answer: First-mover advantage.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. first-mover advantage; patents protect from competition; higher margins from innovative products. 1 mark: explained in the context of Desert Bloom (hospitality). [2]

items.stem: Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd has annual revenue of $50 million and spends $3 million on R&D; the industry average is 6% of revenue. Calculate its R&D as a percentage of revenue and compare it with the industry.
items.markingKey: 3/50 × 100 = 6% [1]; equal to the industry average of 6% [1]. [2]

items.stem: Kiwi Trails Ltd is a private limited company based in Auckland, New Zealand. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours and employs about 90 people. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Explain the stages Kiwi Trails should follow to develop and launch corporate team-building retreats.
items.answer: Points to develop for Kiwi Trails: NPD process: idea generation and screening; concept testing and market research; prototype development and test marketing; commercialisation and launch with an integrated marketing mix.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: NPD process: idea generation and screening. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Kiwi Trails: tourism, about 90 employees, private limited company in New Zealand; bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Kiwi Trails, e.g. concept testing and market research; prototype development and test marketing; commercialisation and launch with an integrated marketing mix. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Lima, Andes Textil SA (family-owned private company) makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. The business has around 320 employees. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Using the case and your own knowledge, evaluate whether Andes Textil should increase its spending on research and development.
items.answer: For: new products and processes; patents and differentiation; long-term growth. Against: high cost and uncertain results; lower short-term profit and dividends; competitors may copy or launch first. Judgement: the decision for Andes Textil depends mainly on the pace of innovation in its industry, and also on its financial resources.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. new products and processes; patents and differentiation; long-term growth; arguments against, e.g. high cost and uncertain results; lower short-term profit and dividends; competitors may copy or launch first. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the pace of innovation in its industry; its financial resources; its ability to protect ideas. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Andes Textil, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Define the term 'pan-global marketing'.
items.answer: Using the same standardised marketing mix (product, brand, promotion) in all countries.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, using the same standardised marketing mix (product, brand, promotion) in all countries. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of entering a foreign market by franchising.
items.answer: Advantage: rapid expansion using the franchisee's capital and local knowledge. Disadvantage: less control over quality and service, which could damage the brand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each with explanation. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business might adapt its products for different countries.
items.answer: Tastes, culture, religion, laws, climate and incomes differ, so a standard product may not meet local needs or regulations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark difference between markets; 1 mark need to adapt. [2]

items.stem: Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Lanka Tea Estates plc, a public limited company in Sri Lanka with about 5,000 employees, grows, processes and packs tea on its own estates. Explain the factors Lanka Tea should consider before selling its products in Russia.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: market research on size, growth and tastes; cultural, legal and political differences; exchange-rate and payment risk; strength of local and global competitors.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: market research on size, growth and tastes. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lanka Tea: agriculture and food, about 5,000 employees, public limited company in Sri Lanka; many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lanka Tea, e.g. cultural, legal and political differences; exchange-rate and payment risk; strength of local and global competitors. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

Mekong Furniture JSC, a joint stock company in Vietnam with about 1,200 employees, makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. Explain the factors Mekong Furniture should consider before selling its products in Australia.
items.answer: Points to develop for Mekong Furniture: market research on size, growth and tastes; cultural, legal and political differences; exchange-rate and payment risk; strength of local and global competitors.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: market research on size, growth and tastes. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Mekong Furniture, e.g. cultural, legal and political differences; exchange-rate and payment risk; strength of local and global competitors. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Recommend the most suitable method for Desert Bloom to enter the market in Saudi Arabia.
items.answer: For: exporting is low risk; joint venture brings local knowledge; own subsidiary gives control. Against: exporting faces tariffs and transport costs; joint ventures share profits; subsidiaries need large investment. Judgement: the decision for Desert Bloom depends mainly on its resources and experience, and also on the size and risk of the market.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. exporting is low risk; joint venture brings local knowledge; own subsidiary gives control; arguments against, e.g. exporting faces tariffs and transport costs; joint ventures share profits; subsidiaries need large investment. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its resources and experience; the size and risk of the market; trade barriers. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Desert Bloom, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which method of entering a foreign market involves the least risk and capital?
items.answer: Exporting through an overseas agent
items.markingKey: Exporting through an overseas agent. Exporting via agents needs little investment, although control is limited.

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd is a private limited company based in Lagos, Nigeria. It produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin and employs about 700 people. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Explain one advantage to Lagos Bites of using a pan-global marketing strategy for packaged snacks.
items.answer: Economies of scale in production and promotion.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. economies of scale in production and promotion; consistent global brand image; simpler management. 1 mark: explained in the context of Lagos Bites (food processing). [2]

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Explain the benefits to Indus Sports of adapting its marketing mix for customers in West Africa.
items.answer: Points to develop for Indus Sports: localisation adapts the mix to local needs; products better meet local tastes and laws; pricing suited to local incomes; promotion that fits culture and language.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: localisation adapts the mix to local needs. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Indus Sports: sports equipment manufacturing, about 950 employees, private limited company in Pakistan; a rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Indus Sports, e.g. products better meet local tastes and laws; pricing suited to local incomes; promotion that fits culture and language. items.stem: Define the term 'market positioning'.
items.answer: The perception customers have of a brand relative to its competitors, e.g. on price and quality, often shown on a perceptual (positioning) map.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the perception customers have of a brand relative to its competitors, e.g. on price and quality, often shown on a perceptual (positioning) map. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a business can use a perceptual map when positioning a new product.
items.answer: It plots customer perceptions of rival brands on two attributes, showing crowded areas and gaps where a new product could be positioned.
items.markingKey: 1 mark plotting perceptions; 1 mark identify gaps/positioning. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between cost leadership and differentiation.
items.answer: Cost leadership aims for the lowest costs in the industry; differentiation offers unique features that justify a higher price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Desert Bloom Hotels plc, a public limited company in the United Arab Emirates with about 3,100 employees, operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels. Explain whether a differentiation strategy would give Desert Bloom a competitive advantage.
items.answer: Points to develop for Desert Bloom: differentiation creates perceived uniqueness; allows premium pricing; reduces price elasticity of demand; requires investment in quality, design and branding.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: differentiation creates perceived uniqueness. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Desert Bloom, e.g. allows premium pricing; reduces price elasticity of demand; requires investment in quality, design and branding. items.stem: Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Lagos Bites Ltd, a private limited company in Nigeria with about 700 employees, produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. Discuss whether Lagos Bites should reposition its brand to target a more upmarket segment.
items.answer: For: higher margins; less price competition; growing affluent segment. Against: loss of existing customers; cost of changing the mix; credibility of the new position. Judgement: the decision for Lagos Bites depends mainly on market research evidence, and also on competitor positions.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Lagos Bites: food processing, about 700 employees, private limited company in Nigeria; rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins). items.stem: Explain why repositioning a brand can be risky.
items.answer: Existing customers may be alienated, the new position may not be believed, and repositioning requires costly changes to the whole marketing mix.
items.markingKey: 1 mark risk; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Based in Santiago, Andina Solar SpA (private limited company) designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The business has around 380 employees. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain two benefits to Andina Solar of following a cost leadership strategy, using the case to support your answer.
items.answer: Lowest unit costs give pricing flexibility; can win price-sensitive segments.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark application to Andina Solar: renewable energy, 380 employees). Points: lowest unit costs give pricing flexibility; can win price-sensitive segments; high margins at average prices; needs large scale and efficiency; vulnerable to rivals with even lower costs; brand may be seen as cheap. [4]

items.stem: Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Savanna Fresh Ltd, a private limited company in Kenya with about 850 employees, grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe. Evaluate whether Savanna Fresh should follow a cost leadership or a differentiation strategy.
items.answer: For: cost leadership suits price-sensitive markets; differentiation allows premium prices; differentiation builds loyalty. Against: cost leadership needs scale; differentiation needs investment and innovation; stuck in the middle risk. Judgement: the decision for Savanna Fresh depends mainly on the size of Savanna Fresh relative to rivals, and also on customer priorities in its market.

AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Savanna Fresh: horticulture, about 850 employees, private limited company in Kenya; its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use). AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the size of Savanna Fresh relative to rivals; customer priorities in its market; its core competencies. items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'marketing budget'?
options: Using the same standardised marketing mix (product, brand, promotion) in all countries.
Allowing a business in another country to use the brand name, products and methods in return for a fee and royalty.
A marketing mix in which the elements (product, price, promotion, place) are consistent with each other and with the target market.
The amount of money allocated to marketing activities over a period, often set as a percentage of sales, by competitor parity or by objective-and-task.
items.answer: The amount of money allocated to marketing activities over a period, often set as a percentage of sales, by competitor parity or by objective-and-task.
items.markingKey: marketing budget: The amount of money allocated to marketing activities over a period, often set as a percentage of sales, by competitor parity or by objective-and-task.

items.stem: Han River Games Co. is a private limited company based in Seoul, South Korea. It develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases and employs about 340 people. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain one advantage to Han River Games of preparing a detailed marketing plan.
items.answer: Clear objectives and coordination.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. clear objectives and coordination; budget controlled and measurable; helps raise finance and evaluate results. 1 mark: explained in the context of Han River Games (video game development). [2]

items.stem: Explain why a marketing plan should include methods of measuring results.
items.answer: Measuring sales, market share or response rates shows whether objectives are being met, so managers can take corrective action and judge value for money.
items.markingKey: 1 mark monitoring; 1 mark corrective action/accountability. [2]

items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. items.answer: Points to develop for Han River Games: a marketing plan sets objectives, strategy, budget and timescales; coordinates the marketing mix for the target segment; allocates the budget to the most effective activities; allows results to be measured against targets.
